chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban, from Abu al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'I gifted a slave girl to the Ka'bah and was given five hundred dinars, so what is your view?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Sell her, then take her price, then stand upon this wall, the wall of the Hijr, then call out and give to everyone who has been cut off (by bandits) and every needy one from the pilgrims.'

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the sacred house in Mecca
key_terms.حَائِطِ الْحِجْرِ: The wall of the Hijr, a semi-circular wall near the Ka'bah
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: Dinar, a gold coin used as currency
key_terms.مُنْقَطَعٍ: One who is cut off or stranded

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave gifted to the Ka'bah and the distribution of their sale price?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the practical application of *tabarru'* (voluntary gift) in Shia jurisprudence, where the donor retains the right to reclaim the gifted item or its value. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) directs the man to liquidate the girl's value and distribute it specifically to *muqtata'* (stranded pilgrims lacking funds) and *muhtaj* (needy pilgrims) near the Hijr, highlighting the Ka'bah's role as a center for social welfare during Hajj.
